dialogues.speaker: Akim
dialogues.text: You get what you pay for. Do you think the work I do is the same as everyone else's?

dialogues.speaker: Harim
dialogues.text: Doing things differently from others doesn't mean your work is worth more.

dialogues.speaker: Harim
dialogues.text: Besides, everyone can learn masonry from the Akasha. What makes you so different anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Akim
dialogues.text: Hah! I wouldn't speak so soon. Akasha's been shut down... and anyway, everyone does things differently!

dialogues.speaker: Harim
dialogues.text: Alright, alright! Let's just say that you win, and your unique craftsmanship is why I buy your goods! Sheesh. If it weren't for the fact that we're old pals, I wouldn't be going out of my way to make sure you're getting business.

dialogues.speaker: Akim
dialogues.text: Hah. The foundational knowledge might be the same, sure, but what gets built upon it is different!

dialogues.speaker: Akim
dialogues.text: Unlike the others, I'm an innovator! I've also tried more kinds of clay...

dialogues.speaker: Harim
dialogues.text: Aha! Caught you, haven't I? Didn't you claim that you weren't asking me for more Mora because you wanted to buy new materials?
